Guarani were brilliant yesterday, left the ground buzzing and walked through the sugarcane fields on the road home. the red soil kicked up by every passing truck, typical interior life. some Japanese agricultural researchers were visiting the plantations. even Indian sugarcane country doesn't have this football-and-agriculture mix

The Strongest had the whole stadium on their feet and the walk home at 3600 metres always leaves you gasping. the altiplano sunset was ridiculous, sky went purple over the canyon. some Swiss mountaineers were at the match, said even their altitude training didn't prepare them for this. Washington NFL games could never have this setting

Victory were shocking. again. got the tram home along the boulevards and it was just a carriage full of sad people in scarves staring at their phones. the arvo sun was warm at least. small mercies. some Italian tourists on the tram looked confused by the collective depression. even Parisian football misery has more style

Phoenix got a decent result but honestly the wind at the ground was the main event. harbour was gorgeous on the walk home, grabbed a flat white from the cafe on the hill to warm up. this city is 90% wind 10% coffee. some American tourists were literally blown sideways. even Scottish coastal towns aren't this gusty

text: Blues had a good result and the sugarcane fields on the drive home were swaying in the tropical evening breeze. stopped at the roadside stall for cassava chips, proper Friday vibes near the sugar mill town. some Australian tourists were at the match. even Hawaiian small-town sport doesn't have this chill island energy

Magpies were in great form and walked out of the ground into perfect autumn weather, the vineyards on the hills catching the last golden light. grabbed a pie from the bakery near the art deco strip, cracking afternoon. some American wine tourists were comparing it to Napa. even the French wine regions don't combine sport and terroir like this

text: Tractor had the stadium bouncing and the carpet bazaar area was absolutely heaving with fans afterward. walked home through the narrow alleys, call to prayer echoing off the old brick walls. love this city on match nights. some Turkish traders were celebrating too. even Egyptian bazaar areas don't buzz like this after football

Partizan put in a shift and the walk home through the riverside fortress area was gorgeous at night. the kafanas were packed and someone was playing accordion on the cobblestones, perfect evening. some Italian tourists were drinking rakija with the locals. even Budapest's riverside nightlife doesn't have this soul

text: Simba were DOMINANT and the ferry terminal area was packed with celebrating fans. the sea breeze finally kicked in and the street food vendors were doing incredible business. perfect evening honestly. some Japanese tourists got caught up in the celebrations. even Brazilian beachside football celebrations aren't this wholesome

America won and the salsa capital went OFF. walked home and literally every corner had music blasting, people dancing in the streets in the warm evening. the sugarcane fields at the edge of town caught the last golden light. this city after a win is something else. some Cuban musicians were jamming with locals. even Brazilian carnival spontaneity can't match this

text: Sport had a frustrating draw but the reef pools at dawn the next morning made up for it. the old colonial centre was gorgeous in the morning light and the tapioca stall near the bridge was already busy. some Portuguese tourists said the architecture reminds them of home. even the Spanish colonial centres aren't this colourful

Eagles had a solid win and the humidity walking out of the ground was absolutely suffocating. the harbour was busy with fishing boats and the betel nut stalls outside were doing a roaring trade. some Australian mining executives were at the match. even Indonesian humidity doesn't prepare you for this level of sweat

Warriors put in a massive shift and the coconut palms swaying in the tropical evening breeze made the walk home gorgeous. grabbed some fresh oka from the market stall, perfect post-match feed. some American Peace Corps volunteers were celebrating with us. even Hawaiian evenings don't feel this community-driven

Giants had the crowd buzzing at the oval and the walk home through the old mining village was quiet, just the sound of bellbirds in the eucalyptus. grabbed a pie from the bakery on the main strip, perfect cold weather food. some British tourists said it reminds them of Cornwall. even the Tasmanian tourism board couldn't sell this place better than a good match day

text: Alianza had the whole neighbourhood celebrating, walked home past the volcano views and the pupusa vendors were doing incredible business. the evening breeze coming down from the highlands finally made the heat bearable. some American embassy staff were at the match. even Mexican football celebrations don't have this volcano backdrop

Rovers scraped a win and the post-match kava session near the ground was exactly what I needed. the tropical humidity hadn't let up even at sunset and the palm-lined road home was sticky and warm. some Australian backpackers joined the kava circle. even the Indonesian island evenings my mate describes aren't this relaxed
